title: Lumora "Dewdrop" lip-oil PDP set: neutralize eight mixed-light iPhone captures to an in-frame grey card, cut every bottle out on pure white, recolor the oil into three shade colorways, and data-merge an authored shade card

source.reference: Blind Box Packaging Design (PART A — Product Photo Retouching)

grounding_note: Grounded in the Upwork hourly brief "Blind Box Packaging Design", PART A — PRODUCT PHOTO RETOUCHING. VERBATIM phrases quoted from the brief: "Clean up iPhone product photos I'll provide of one physical sample"; "Maintain consistent lighting, shadow, and gold-clasp detail across all"; "internal highlights and shadows should shift naturally with each color". The brief also asks to "Cut out the case on a transparent background, 300 DPI" and to "Recolor the case + wrist strap into additional color variants" — the identical real-world intent is kept: one physical sample shot on a phone (here across several mixed-light sessions for the product carousel), neutralized to a common look, cut out clean on a marketplace-compliant white background, then recolored into a shade lineup with consistent lighting/shadow and translucent-material highlights preserved and a metallic detail (the brushed-gold collar and cap) held constant across every variant. The original brief bundles this photo-retouch job with an out-of-scope Illustrator dieline rebuild (PART B, from-scratch vector packaging on a manufacturer's dieline); PART B is dropped because from-scratch vector layout composition is not in connector scope. STRENGTHENED vs the prior spec: the prior version fanned ONE raw shot into eight saturated shades (a batch amputated to a single hero, and a recolor of an effectively colorless oil into deeply saturated brand hues that image_adjust_hsl cannot actually perform — a hue-rotation of near-zero-chroma pixels), and it asserted 'identical across all 8' with no reference and no measurable target (audit group G6). Rebuilt so the batch is restored to eight genuinely differently-lit captures each carrying a physical in-frame three-patch neutral grey card (the free, gradeable consistency target), the shade recolor is retargeted onto a bottle whose oil already carries a real warm-coral chroma so the moves stay inside image_adjust_hsl's realistic within-family range (coral held, a bounded hop to rose, a strong desaturate to a bare sheer), and the endpoint is an agent-owned authored artifact — a genuine InDesign single-record shade-card data-merge — rather than a locally-typeset note. FICTIONAL / IP-CLEAN: the real "Mogano Jewelry & Accessories" jewelry-case brand is replaced with a fictional beauty-cosmetics brand, Lumora Beauty Co., and its "Dewdrop" glass-bottle lip oil; the translucent-gemstone material becomes translucent lip oil in frosted glass and the gold clasp becomes a brushed-gold collar and cap. Adobe/Photoshop/InDesign and the marketplace-white-background convention are referenced as tools/format only; no marketplace, company, person, org, product, or trademark is named.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight mixed-light iPhone captures of one lip-oil bottle to the three-patch grey card each one carries so the carousel shares one white point, cut every bottle out onto pure white, then generate three oil-only shade colorways from the cleanest hero with the brushed-gold collar and cap held identical, prep and vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge the client's authored InDesign shade-card template into one press-ready PDF, one page per shade.
full_brief: Lumora Beauty Co. is launching "Dewdrop," a warm-tinted lip oil in a frosted-glass dropper bottle with a brushed-gold collar and a matching gold cap. We are NOT reshooting. We photographed our ONE physical sample on an iPhone across several sessions to build the product carousel, and the eight frames we are handing you look like they came from eight different shoots — some read cool and blue, some warm, one picked up a sickly cast from the shop lights, a couple are too dark or too bright, one is flat and muddy. Every frame has our three-patch neutral grey card (a light / mid / dark card) lying on the white sweep in one corner; that card is your ground truth. Job one, the carousel: make these read as ONE product on a pure-white PDP. Neutralize each frame to the grey card it carries so the whole set lands on one shared white point, then build and hold one clean, bright, restrained-contrast e-commerce house look across all eight — the three grey patches must read as true neutral (no blue, no amber, no green/magenta), the mid patch must sit at the same mid-grey across the set, the white sweep must stay clean and below clipping, and the darkest patch must stay off pure black. Then cut the bottle out cleanly and place it on a pure white #FFFFFF background — marketplace-compliant, no baked drop-shadow, product centered with a little margin — and deliver each at 2000x2000. Here is where our last editor failed, and it is your call, not ours: the eight did NOT start from the same place, so there is no single correction that fixes them — a move that rescues one frame drives another further off. Judge each frame on its own card, work out what is actually wrong with it, and dial it its own correction. Do NOT reach for one global white-balance number, do NOT copy one frame's settings onto the rest, and do NOT auto-tone each frame to look fine on its own — auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram, so the casts will not agree and the set will visibly fail to match at the card, and we will reject it. And be careful: the oil really is a warm coral, so if a frame's card already reads neutral, do not chase an imagined blue cast and cool the product's real color away. When you are done, tell us the final correction you applied to each of the eight frames — the temperature and tint direction and amount, the exposure and highlight/shadow moves, the contrast, clarity and vibrance you dialed — so we can confirm each frame got its own move rather than one recipe copied across the batch. Job two, the shade lineup, no reshoot: from your cleanest hero shot, give us three colorways of the SAME bottle for the launch page — the original warm Coral Nectar, a soft Rose Quartz, and a Bare Sheer wash. Only the oil inside the glass may change color. The brushed-gold collar, the gold cap, the frosted glass, the lighting and shadow, and the white background must stay IDENTICAL across all three — only the oil shifts. The tint has to read as real translucent oil, with the internal highlights and the light passing through the glass shifting naturally with the color, NOT a flat paint fill and NOT a color that bleeds onto the metal or the sweep. Job three: our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper — get it clean and razor-sharp so it does not look like a fuzzy scan when printed. Finally, build the piece: we have hand-built an InDesign shade-card template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the product shot, one for the wordmark at the top of the card), and we are giving you the shade lineup as a data file; merge them so every shade gets its own card page with its copy bound verbatim, its matching colorway image dropped in, and the crisp wordmark dropped into the header, then hand back one press-ready shade-card PDF — one page per shade. Bind our copy exactly as written; do not rewrite it.

inputs.name: dewdrop_sample_captures_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-resolution iPhone captures (each ~4032x3024 px straight off the phone, before any crop) of ONE physical sample: a frosted-glass dropper bottle of lip oil standing upright on a seamless white studio sweep, with a brushed-gold metal collar at the neck, a gold dropper cap, and inside a clearly WARM-CORAL translucent oil showing real internal highlights and light passing through the frosted glass. In one corner of every frame, lying flat on the sweep, a small three-patch neutral photographic reference card (light grey / mid grey / dark grey patches side by side, no color tint on the card itself), clearly visible and uncropped. The SAME bottle is shot from carousel angles (front, three-quarter, macro of the collar, top-down flat-lay) across several sessions under mismatched light, deliberately imperfect: (1) three-quarter view under cool window-shade light, distinctly cool/blue so its card skews bluish, frame tilted ~3 degrees; (2) front view under a warm tungsten desk lamp, amber cast so its card skews warm; (3) flat-lay under mixed shop fluorescents so the whole frame carries a sickly GREEN cast and its card skews green; (4) three-quarter view under near-neutral daylight where the warm-coral oil is the REAL product color and the card already reads neutral (no white-balance error to fix); (5) macro of the collar and dropper, clearly UNDEREXPOSED and dull, the white sweep reading grey and the card sitting dark; (6) front view slightly OVEREXPOSED and warm, specular glints on the glass near clipping and the card skewing bright/amber; (7) three-quarter view, flat, muddy and low-contrast with a faint cool haze, frame tilted ~4 degrees; (8) a clean, near-neutral three-quarter hero view, well exposed with only a slight cast, the bottle centered with room around it. Every shot has real glass reflections, condensation, brushed-metal texture and a soft contact shadow, candid documentary phone-photo look, cluttered nothing else in frame, no studio gloss, no CGI. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs named capture_01.jpg ... capture_08.jpg.
inputs.realism_notes: One physical sample shot many times for the carousel, deliberately mismatched so the neutralization is genuine cross-asset work, not a single hero. The eight need DIFFERENT corrections that all converge on the in-frame grey card: capture_01 warm-to-neutral (cool/blue), capture_02 cool-to-neutral (warm tungsten), capture_03 a TINT-axis push toward MAGENTA (the green fluorescent cast a temperature move can never clear), capture_05 a large exposure-rescue lift, capture_06 a highlight pull-down plus cool, capture_07 contrast/clarity haze recovery plus a mild warm nudge, capture_08 only a small nudge. capture_04 is the TRAP: it was shot under neutral light and its card ALREADY reads neutral, so the correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match brightness) — an agent that batch-applies a 'warm the cool cast' or 'cool an imagined blue' move here neutralizes the card off-neutral and strips the coral oil's real color. capture_08 is the cleanest and is the recolor HERO. The bottle carries TWO warm regions that sit in nearly the SAME hue band — the brushed-gold collar/cap and the warm-coral oil — so a hue-band or whole-image recolor drags the gold along with the oil; only a semantic, object-level selection of the oil isolates it, and the coral oil's real chroma is what lets a bounded within-family hue move (coral->rose) and a strong desaturate (coral->bare sheer) stay inside image_adjust_hsl's realistic range. File names are a neutral capture_NN scheme with a single extension so nothing telegraphs which frame is the trap, which is the hero, or which correction each needs. REAL-CAMERA ~4032x3024 capture (NOT a ~1024-1536 px AI-gen raster) so every 2000x2000 white-bg crop is DOWNSCALE ONLY and the colorway images place into the shade card at ~300 DPI without any upscaling.

inputs.name: lumora_shade_lineup.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns shade_name,finish,copy,hue_note,@image,@Wordmark holding exactly 3 shade rows for the Dewdrop lip-oil launch: Coral Nectar (finish 'warm coral', a one-line marketing note, hue_note 'the as-shot warm coral oil, held'), Rose Quartz (finish 'soft rose', marketing note, hue_note 'a soft rose-pink within the warm-red family'), Bare Sheer (finish 'clear sheer wash', marketing note, hue_note 'a near-clear low-chroma sheer'). copy is a short launch-page product line the merge binds verbatim. The @image column names the matching prepped colorway file the editor produces (e.g. @dewdrop_coral_white.jpg) so the one-file-per-row merge drops each colorway image into that shade's card. The @Wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @dewdrop_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every card. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<shade_name>>,<<finish>>,<<copy>>,<<hue_note>> and the two @-image-path columns @image and @Wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: The client's shade lineup as a data handoff; drives which colorway each card page lists and binds the marketing copy verbatim. hue_note states the TARGET look of each shade as a GOAL only (held / a soft rose / a near-clear sheer) — it does NOT say which raw capture becomes the hero, which region to select, or which tool to use; the recolor decision and the naming of each @image file are the agent's, produced by its own triage, never handed to it in this file. Three rows => the merge must produce exactly three card pages. @Wordmark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all three rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark a connector-doable path onto every card via the merge rather than banned free-form placement (mirrors the two-image-column datamerge pattern).

inputs.name: lumora_shadecard_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD portrait shade card — ONE shade per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<shade_name>>, <<finish>>, <<copy>>, <<hue_note>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a hero product-image frame bound to @image (the matching colorway image) and a masthead image frame at the top of the card bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized Lumora wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, both the colorway image and the wordmark reach the page ONLY as merge binds through these two image frames — never dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record shade card is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. TWO image columns (@image, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's colorway image AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark has a real, connector-doable path onto every card without any free-form placement.

inputs.name: lumora_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Lumora' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a light modern serif with a small dewdrop mark, deep charcoal letters. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper field and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast/crispness, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering.

inputs.name: lumora_house_look_target.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED one-page house-look target sheet (supplied by the client, not model-generated, and NOT a loadable develop preset): states the Lumora Dewdrop PDP acceptance target in words and reference swatches only — every product hero sits on pure white #FFFFFF at 2000x2000 px; the three-patch neutral grey card must read neutral (equal R/G/B, no residual tint) on every neutralized frame; the mid grey patch must sit at a consistent mid-grey brightness across the set; the white sweep must stay clean and below clipping (no blown paper); the darkest patch must stay off pure black; overall a clean bright e-commerce look with gentle contrast, enough clarity to resolve the frosted glass and brushed metal, and a modest vibrance lift so the product pops on white without oversaturating; and the brushed-gold collar and cap (accent #C9A24B) must stay unchanged across every shade colorway. It is a target to hit by eye, not a preset to apply.
inputs.realism_notes: Deliberately a written/visual TARGET, not an .xmp or a built-in preset name. The agent must BUILD the house look from primitive tone controls and hold it identical across the batch, neutralizing each frame to the in-frame grey card BY EYE — there is no preset to lean on. This is what makes the look agent-authored rather than a preset pick. The numeric tolerances on the card belong to the grader, not to any step the agent performs. Read as a written brief (words + swatches), not measured with any pixel tool.

outputs.name: dewdrop_pdp_whitebg_x8
outputs.spec: Eight product images of the one bottle, one per capture, each neutralized on its own terms to the in-frame three-patch grey card — the cool frames warmed, the warm frames cooled, the green fluorescent frame pushed on the tint axis toward magenta, the underexposed frame exposure-rescued, the overexposed frame highlight-recovered, the muddy frame contrast-recovered, and the genuinely-warm neutral-light frame held — then the same authored house look (gentle contrast + clarity + modest vibrance, built from primitive adjustments, no preset, no auto-tone) held identical across all eight, the bottle cut out and placed on a pure white #FFFFFF background (no baked drop-shadow, centered with margin) at 2000x2000 px. Delivered as the eight white-background product crops (grey card cropped OUT) ALONGSIDE their RETAINED pre-cutout neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED pre-cutout neutralized master of each frame (its grey card still present) — the three patches read true-neutral within a tight channel-spread tolerance, the mid patch matches a shared mid-grey level across all eight, the white sweep stays below the clip ceiling and the darkest patch stays off pure black, and each product's genuine color is not forced off; (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered white-background 2000x2000 crop (grey card fully cropped OUT, background pure #FFFFFF). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed product crop. The grader measures these on the output; the agent does not.

outputs.name: dewdrop_colorways_x3
outputs.spec: Three white-background colorways of the SAME hero bottle at 2000x2000 px on pure white #FFFFFF: Coral Nectar (the as-shot warm coral oil, held), Rose Quartz (the oil shifted to a soft rose-pink), and Bare Sheer (the oil pulled to a near-clear low-chroma sheer wash). Each recolor is confined to a semantic selection of ONLY the translucent oil inside the glass via masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl (a bounded within-family hue nudge and/or a strong desaturate, riding the oil's existing luminosity) so the internal highlights and the light through the frosted glass shift naturally with the color — no flat fill, no whole-image overlay, no halo. Acceptance (grader-checked): across all three the brushed-gold collar, the gold cap, the frosted glass, the lighting/shadow and the white background are pixel-identical to the hero base (only the oil differs), the oil's original highlight/translucency structure survives rather than being flat-filled, and each shade reads as a plausible translucent oil rather than a paint chip.

outputs.name: dewdrop_shade_card.pdf
outputs.spec: One press-ready portrait shade-card PDF, exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge as exactly THREE pages — one single-record card per shade row (page-count = row-count = 3). Each card binds its shade_name/finish/copy/hue_note verbatim from the shade lineup with its matching colorway image dropped into the hero product frame (via @image) and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the masthead frame (via @Wordmark) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality. Acceptance (grader-checked): page-count equals row-count (3); if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

outputs.name: dewdrop_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the Lumora wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground and no skew.

outputs.name: grade_parameter_report
outputs.spec: A short written report the agent authors and returns listing, per capture (capture_01..capture_08), the final correction it APPLIED — the temperature and tint direction and amount, the exposure and highlight/shadow moves, and the contrast/clarity/vibrance it dialed — and naming which axis carried each frame (warm-to-neutral, cool-to-neutral, magenta tint for the green frame, exposure-rescue for the dark frame, highlight-recovery for the bright frame, contrast recovery for the muddy frame, and white-balance HELD for the genuinely-warm neutral-light frame). This is an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement: the agent knows these values because it set them by eye. Acceptance (grader-checked): the eight reported corrections are non-identical and their directions match each frame's stated cast — in particular the green frame carries a tint (not a temperature) move, the warm and cool frames move in opposite temperature directions, and the neutral-light frame is reported as WB held (not corrected).

connector_workflow.note: Triage: this frame is tilted ~3 degrees, so level it first (only the tilted captures 01 and 07 get straightened; deciding which is part of the job). image_auto_straighten is the ONLY tool that rectifies a tilt.

Cool/blue window-shade cast: judge the bluish card by eye and WARM the temperature toward neutral (dial and record the temp; add a touch of tint only if the card also skews green), lift exposure/shadows out of the flat baseline, then lay in the authored house look built here from primitives against the written target — gentle contrast, clarity to resolve the frosted glass and brushed metal, whites held below the clip ceiling so the sweep stays clean, blacks seated just off pure black, modest vibrance. Goal: the three grey patches look neutral by eye and the mid patch reads at the set mid-grey. This full-frame neutralized master (grey card still in frame) is RETAINED for neutrality grading. Single authored adjustments call — not a preset, not auto-tone (replaces the prior spec's deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature).

Cut the bottle out of the sweep and place it on a pure white ground in one move: image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) — the sanctioned white-ground path (NOT select->invert->fill, NOT image_fill_area). This isolates the outer background only and removes the grey card (which sits on the sweep) along with it, so the delivered crop carries no card; the bottle has no enclosed interior negative space to punch, so no enclosed-hole knockout is claimed.

Crop and resize to the 2000x2000 px square PDP frame, bottle centered with margin, grey card fully cropped OUT. This card-removed white-bg crop is the delivered product image; neutrality is graded on the retained cap01_neutralized master, and card-exclusion is the separate check on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract' (never 'expand'), downscale-only from the ~4032 px source, never enlarging.

Warm tungsten desk-lamp cast — the OPPOSITE temperature move to capture_01: COOL the temperature toward the same neutral card target, hold exposure, then apply the identical house-look contrast/clarity/vibrance so it matches the set. Warming this frame (as capture_01 needed) would drive it further amber — judging THIS card is what tells the agent to reverse direction. Retained master; report the cooling amount dialed.
Cut out onto pure white #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); card removed with the sweep.
Crop/resize to the 2000x2000 white PDP frame, card cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Green fluorescent flat-lay — the TINT-axis frame. This one does NOT move on the warm/cool axis: judge the green card by eye and push TINT toward MAGENTA to neutralize it (with only a small temperature trim), then seat the mid/whites/blacks on the shared target and apply the identical house look. A temperature-only correction, a single global WB copied from another frame, or an auto-tone pass cannot clear a green cast at all — this frame's card would stay green while the others look fixed, the visible failure this gate catches. Retained master; report the magenta tint amount and confirm it is a tint (not a temperature) move.
Cut out onto pure white #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}).
Crop/resize to the 2000x2000 white PDP frame, card cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. Shot under near-neutral daylight, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral and the warm-coral oil is the REAL product color. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set and apply the house look. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' move used on capture_01 or 'cools an imagined blue cast' will neutralize the card off-neutral and strip the coral the client is selling. Decision is driven by THIS card, not the batch. Retained master; report that WB was HELD.
Cut out onto pure white #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}).
Crop/resize to the 2000x2000 white PDP frame, card cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Underexposed macro of the collar — the exposure-rescue frame: a large exposure + shadow lift to bring the grey sweep up toward white and the card up to legibility, held in check by pulling highlights/whites so the recovered sweep does not blow past the clip ceiling and the dark patch stays off pure black, plus a slight warm toward neutral and the house-look contrast/clarity/vibrance. The magnitude of this lift is unique to this frame; copying any other frame's exposure here visibly under- or over-shoots. Retained master; report the exposure/shadow/highlight moves dialed.
Cut out onto pure white #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}).
Crop/resize to the 2000x2000 white PDP frame, card cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Overexposed and warm: PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the near-clipped glass glints and the bright card, then COOL to neutralize the card to the shared white point — opposite tonal AND WB direction from the underexposed frame, proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. House-look character to match. Retained master; report the highlight pull and cooling applied.
Cut out onto pure white #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}).
Crop/resize to the 2000x2000 white PDP frame, card cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~4 degrees and muddy — level it first before grading.

Muddy, low-contrast, faint-cool haze: the dominant move is contrast + clarity to defeat the haze and resolve the frosted glass, plus a mild warm nudge to neutralize the faint cool card; land the mid patch on the shared mid-grey without letting the added contrast crush the dark patch or blow the sweep. House-look vibrance to match. Retained master; report the contrast/clarity and the mild warm applied.
Cut out onto pure white #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}).
Crop/resize to the 2000x2000 white PDP frame, card cropped out. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

The clean hero, near-neutral: only a small WB nudge to land on the shared white point plus the identical house look — over-correcting would push it off the matched set. This is the cleanest frame and becomes the recolor hero. Retained master; report the (small) move.
Cut the hero out onto pure white #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); card removed with the sweep.

Crop/resize the hero to the 2000x2000 white PDP frame, card cropped out. This clean white-bg hero is BOTH the eighth PDP delivery frame AND the base every colorway is built from (build once, re-hue) — it is also the Coral Nectar colorway as-shot, so the agent hands it forward as the coral colorway image. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Semantic selection of ONLY the translucent oil inside the glass: prompt 'the translucent liquid oil inside the frosted-glass dropper bottle', deliberately excluding the brushed-gold collar, the gold cap and the glass rim. This is the triage crux — the warm-coral oil and the brushed-gold collar/cap sit in nearly the SAME warm hue band, so a hue-based selection or a whole-image color tool cannot separate them (it would drag the gold with the oil); only a semantic, object-level selection isolates the oil. Returns a maskURI reused for every recolor so the metal and white background never change. Not a hue or coordinate selection.

Rose Quartz masked recolor pass 1 (consumes the hero base AND the oil mask): within the selection only, nudge the warm-coral oil a bounded hop toward rose-pink through the red band — a small within-family hue shift well under image_adjust_hsl's ~90-degree ceiling (NOT a near-complementary rotation) — while the oil's existing luminosity carries its internal highlights and the light through the glass so it reads as tinted translucent oil, not flat paint. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path the connector exposes; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image with no mask (it would tint the gold collar, the cap and the white background too) and image_fill_area is a flat solid fill that would erase the oil's translucency — both are the exact 'flat fill / bleeds onto the metal' the brief rejects. Gold collar/cap and #FFFFFF background outside the mask untouched.

Rose Quartz masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): trim the residual chroma and settle the saturation/luminance so the oil lands on a soft, believable rose rather than a candy pink or a washed grey, still riding the original luminosity so the highlights and glass translucency stay natural. A single pass can overshoot; this dependent second pass places the final shade. Full 2000x2000 white-bg colorway image the agent names for the merge (@image = dewdrop_rose_white.jpg).

Bare Sheer masked recolor (same oil mask, off the same clean base): within the selection only, pull the coral oil's saturation DOWN hard toward a near-clear low-chroma sheer wash with a slight luminance lift — a strong desaturate, squarely inside image_adjust_hsl's realistic range (it desaturates strongly) and NOT a hue rotation, so the oil keeps only the faintest warmth and reads as a bare translucent tint. Gold collar/cap and white background untouched. Full 2000x2000 white-bg colorway image the agent names for the merge (@image = dewdrop_sheer_white.jpg). The Coral Nectar colorway is hero_white_base as-shot (dewdrop_coral_white.jpg) — no recolor call, only its own naming.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits ~2 degrees rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward white so the charcoal lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The 'Lumora' serif has open counters that read fine as transparent on the light card ground.

difficulty_rationale: Depth over breadth: 39 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grade/mask/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), well above the >=10-call / >=6-distinct-tool floor even after stripping the two upload steps and the auto-straighten auto-ops. The core is NOT a repeated recipe. First, eight differently-lit captures of one bottle must all converge on a single measurable target — the in-frame three-patch grey card — with each frame needing its OWN reasoned, often opposite-direction correction (warm cooled, cool warmed, a magenta tint move on the green frame that no temperature move can make, an exposure-rescue of unique magnitude, a highlight-recovery, a contrast/clarity recovery, and one frame where the correct move is to HOLD white balance because the warmth is real product), so a blanket batch correction or per-frame auto-tone visibly fails at the card. The house look is authored from primitive tone controls (contrast/clarity/vibrance/whites/blacks) and held identical, not picked from a preset and not delegated to auto-tone. Second, the shade recolor is a genuine constraint-reasoning + triage problem: the warm-coral oil and the brushed-gold collar/cap sit in the same warm hue band, so the oil can only be isolated semantically (image_select_by_prompt on the liquid, never a hue selection), then recolored with masked luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl within its realistic range — a bounded within-family hop to rose (two dependent passes) and a strong desaturate to a bare sheer — because the connector's whole-image color tools would tint the gold and the white ground and its fill tool would flatten the oil's translucency. Third, a prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white scan and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record shade-card template make the endpoint an agent-owned designed artifact rather than a punt. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used; image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) is the sanctioned white-ground path (no select->invert->fill, no fill_area); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature is replaced by image_apply_adjustments. No step asks the agent to measure a pixel.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a craft decision with a visible failure mode, not a self-measurement): the eight captures start on divergent casts across the temperature, tint and exposure axes, and the agent must dial each frame its own correction BY EYE to the in-frame three-patch grey card — warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed, the green fluorescent frame pushed toward MAGENTA on the tint axis, the dark frame exposure-rescued, the bright frame highlight-recovered, the muddy frame contrast-recovered, and the neutral-light frame HELD. The naive path — one global white-balance number, one frame's settings copied across the batch, or auto-tone per frame — visibly fails to match at the card: auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram so the casts never agree, a temperature-only or single-global move cannot touch the green cast at all (its card stays green while the rest look fixed), and correcting the neutral-light frame at all strips the coral the client is selling. The failure is legible on the retained card-bearing master without any pixel readout, and the required grade_parameter_report — an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement — exposes identical-params laziness directly. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target — eight differently-lit shots all neutralized to the same in-frame grey card and the same mid/whites/blacks, which demands the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT requires DIFFERENT per-frame corrections across three axes, plus the discipline to leave the genuinely-warm frame alone; (2) constraint-reasoning + triage in the recolor — the coral oil and the brushed-gold collar/cap share a hue band, so the oil can only be isolated with a semantic object selection and recolored with masked luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl passes inside the tool's realistic range (a bounded coral->rose hop, a strong coral->bare-sheer desaturate), never a hue-band pull, a whole-image overlay, or a flat fill; (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, off-white, margin-padded wordmark scan before vectorize. THE TRAP: capture_04's warmth is real product color and its card already reads neutral, so batch-applying a 'warm the cool cast' correction (or cooling an imagined blue cast) neutralizes its card off-neutral and strips the coral; and on the recolor side, reaching for the obvious color tools — a whole-image overlay or a hue-band shift toward rose — drags the same-hue gold collar and cap pink, or a flat fill kills the oil's translucency, exactly the 'bleeds onto the metal / flat fill' the brief rejects. A second merge trap: a multi-record grid catalog or a convert_pdf_to_indd template both fail to bind/produce; only the supplied single-record authored .indd merges. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, decoupled so nothing is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey-card neutrality (channel spread within tolerance) and one shared white point with mid/whites/blacks on target, evaluated on the eight RETAINED pre-cutout neutralized masters (card still in frame), never on a card-removed crop; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the eight delivered 2000x2000 white-bg crops (card cropped OUT, ground pure #FFFFFF); (c) across the three colorways the gold collar/cap, glass, lighting and white ground are pixel-identical to the hero base with only the oil changed and its translucency intact; (d) the delivered grade_parameter_report lists non-identical per-frame corrections whose directions match each frame's cast (a tint move on the green frame, opposite temperature moves on warm vs cool frames, WB held on the neutral-light frame); and (e) the shade-card PDF page-count equals the row-count (3) — so 'matched' and 'consistent' are checkable rather than asserted, and the agent supplies parameters it applied rather than values it read.
